message.content:
You are an EFFICIENCY reviewer for a code-quality cleanup pass (not a bug hunt). Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim

Get the diff under review (F8: andes-sim `run --model accurate`, a C++20 driver in driver/):
  git -C /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim diff HEAD~2..HEAD -- driver/ tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f8.sh

Your single angle: EFFICIENCY. Flag wasted work this diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O, independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or a hot path. Name the cheaper alternative.

Context that matters: discover_engines() (driver/engine_registry.cpp) scans a directory and spawns `<bin> --describe` as a SUBPROCESS for every candidate binary (5s timeout each). That is the expensive operation in this diff's path.

Specifically scrutinize:
- driver/cmd_run.cpp run_accurate: it calls discover_engines() (spawns a --describe subprocess per Verilator build) and only THEN does run_standalone() validate the positional ELF. So `run --model accurate` (no ELF) or `run --model accurate a b` (extra positional) pays the full discovery cost before failing on a CLI error that needs no engine at all. Is that wasted work worth reordering? Weigh against code duplication (the positional check lives in run_standalone). Note F7's run_fast deliberately AVOIDS discovery by resolving builtin_qemu() directly - is there an analogous cheap path here?
- driver/engine_registry.hpp resolve_accurate_engine: any redundant passes over `engines` (it's a small vector, so this is low-stakes - only flag if clearly wasteful)?
- tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f8.sh: the real-vsim layer uses `timeout 45` on a fixture known not to terminate (always burns up to 45s). Independent setup that could be cheaper? (This is a manual dev smoke test, not CI - weigh accordingly.)

For EACH finding return: `file`, `line` (from the diff), a one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what work is wasted and the cheaper alternative). Only flag real waste; a few microseconds over a 5-element vector is not worth a finding. Be concise - a short bulleted list, nothing else.

content.text: Let me pin exact line numbers for the citations.

EFFICIENCY review of the F8 diff (`run --model accurate`):

- **`driver/cmd_run.cpp:67` — discovery runs before CLI validation.** `run_accurate` calls `discover_engines()` first; the positional-ELF check (`empty` / `size>1`) lives in `run_standalone`, reached only after. So `run --model accurate` (no ELF) or `run --model accurate a b` (extra positional) pays the full discovery cost — a `verilator/build` dir scan plus one `<bin> --describe` fork/exec/JSON-parse per `sim_*` binary, run **sequentially**, each with a 5s timeout (`kDescribeTimeoutMs`) — only to fail on a CLI error that needs no engine. Worst case N*5s of subprocess spawning to print "missing ELF". Cheaper: hoist the engine-independent positional-count check ahead of `discover_engines()`. To avoid duplicating `run_standalone`'s two `fprintf` branches, factor them into a tiny `check_one_elf(cli, model)` helper and call it at the top of `run_accurate`. F7's `run_fast` dodges this for free because `builtin_qemu()` spawns nothing; `accurate` has no such cheap path for a *successful* run, but the CLI-error case is exactly where discovery is pure waste.

- **`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f8.sh:106` — `timeout 45` always burns the full 45s.** The fixture `handoff_roundtrip.elf` provably never terminates standalone (no exit path without QEMU semihosting, per the script's own header), so vsim loops, never prints "N cycles simulated", the grep fails, and the run always hits rc=124 after the full 45s. The cycle-line "ok" branch is therefore currently unreachable; layer 3 always spends 45s wall time to print a `[skip]`, adding no deterministic coverage beyond layer 2 (which the header already calls "the deterministic proof"). Cheaper: cap at a few seconds — the skip message only claims to prove "vsim launched and is running," which a ~5s timeout establishes equally. It's a manual dev smoke test (low frequency), so low stakes, but the 45s is guaranteed-wasted on every invocation.

- **`driver/engine_registry.hpp` `resolve_accurate_engine` — not a finding.** The extra `accurate_ids()` pass (lines 63, 81) fires only on the error branches (no-match / ambiguous); both success paths are single-pass over a ~5-element vector. Not worth changing.
